segments.section: Sacred inheritance and rival continuations
segments.text: Sacred inheritance and rival continuations

segments.section: A rival can be threatening because the inheritance is shared
segments.text: A rival can be threatening because the inheritance is shared

segments.section: A rival can be threatening because the inheritance is shared
segments.text: The book's organizing hypothesis is not that religious differences disappear when similarities are found. It is that some of the strongest conflicts arise among communities that claim overlapping scriptures, ancestors, teachers and sacred authority. A rival is not always an unrelated outsider. The rival can be another claimant to the very inheritance by which a community recognizes itself.

segments.section: A rival can be threatening because the inheritance is shared
segments.text: Rival continuations preserve some elements of an inheritance while reorganizing others and disputing who has the right to do so. A community can understand another as a successor, a correction, a distortion or an appropriation. I examine these perspectives in specific sources rather than assign a uniform belief to every member of a modern religion.

segments.section: A rival can be threatening because the inheritance is shared
segments.text: The argument therefore refuses two easy compressions. One says the traditions are wholly separate systems that happen to resemble each other. The other says they are all really the same and their disagreements are superficial. The inquiry concerns the actual transformations: what is retained, what is contested, what is replaced and how that change becomes legitimate in the eyes of those who make it.

segments.section: Legitimacy consists of several things that can come apart
segments.text: Legitimacy consists of several things that can come apart

segments.section: Legitimacy consists of several things that can come apart
segments.text: The seed's key example is temple legitimacy. Sacred location, priestly descent, ritual practice, calendar, accepted texts and the authority to interpret them can be bound together, but they are not one property. A community could preserve a priestly claim while disputing a location. It could share scriptures while rejecting a later canon. It could maintain an inherited calendar that places its festivals out of step with those of its neighbors.

segments.section: Legitimacy consists of several things that can come apart
segments.text: The Library of Congress's accounts of the Calendrical Document and Torah Precepts show why calendar and ritual differences deserve separate attention in the Scrolls inquiry. They describe disputes over practices and a framework for separation. They do not establish every proposed relationship between Qumran and later groups. Their value here is narrower and concrete: apparently shared religious language can coexist with consequential differences in practice.

segments.section: Legitimacy consists of several things that can come apart
segments.text: The Samaritan inquiry applies the same decomposition to wording, canon and sacred place. El in Egypt asks what continuity a divine name supports. The Kenite hypothesis asks about the transmission of worship. These should be related investigations rather than steps in a single automatically proved genealogy.

segments.section: Egypt is not one undifferentiated route
segments.text: Egypt is not one undifferentiated route

segments.section: Egypt is not one undifferentiated route
segments.text: The source seed places Elephantine, Leontopolis and the proposed Egyptian setting of later Jewish and Christian transmission in conversation. The argument is comparative: a later authority may judge an earlier or parallel sanctuary illegitimate using criteria the earlier community did not share. That creates a question about how retrospective boundaries are imposed on a varied past.

segments.section: Egypt is not one undifferentiated route
segments.text: The locations and periods must still retain their own records. Evidence about a Judean sanctuary, a priestly temple claim and the preservation of a Coptic manuscript has different implications. A shared geographical label cannot substitute for a route connecting the people, documents or practices involved. The point of a richer wiki is to retain those distinctions while investigating their relations, not to turn Egypt into a single explanatory box.

segments.section: Egypt is not one undifferentiated route
segments.text: This makes the TOR-to-Gnostic investigation a particularly important test. It proposes mechanisms for continuity across displacement and changes of vocabulary. Those mechanisms can be compared with the evidence one by one. If a specific connection fails, the record should show what that changes in the reconstruction instead of discarding every other comparison or quietly replacing the failed premise.

segments.section: Historical continuity and moral faithfulness are different questions
segments.text: Historical continuity and moral faithfulness are different questions

segments.section: Historical continuity and moral faithfulness are different questions
segments.text: A genuine institutional lineage does not guarantee that an institution behaves faithfully to its stated values. Conversely, someone outside the lineage can act in accordance with those values without thereby proving that their own institution has an alternative historical pedigree. Separating these questions prevents ancestry from becoming a substitute for moral judgment.

segments.section: Historical continuity and moral faithfulness are different questions
segments.text: The comparison of power and repair within scripture establishes why this matters. Religious language can authorize violence or challenge the misuse of power. The existence of that conflict inside an inheritance means that receiving it does not eliminate the work of interpretation. Which voice becomes normative, and what justifies that decision?

segments.section: Historical continuity and moral faithfulness are different questions
segments.text: This question also changes how the book approaches borrowing. A teaching may acquire value through a later interpretation without that interpretation having been the earliest meaning. A historical claim about direct transmission still needs historical evidence. A philosophical argument about the value of an interpretation needs reasons appropriate to that argument. Neither is improved by disguising itself as the other.

segments.section: From inherited text to inward authority
segments.text: From inherited text to inward authority

segments.section: From inherited text to inward authority
segments.text: An inheritance is not only stored in a library or an institution. It can become part of the way a person imagines possible actions, recognizes obligations and judges themselves. In Christ as an inner model, remembered teaching becomes an active reference in a decision.

segments.section: From inherited text to inward authority
segments.text: The content matters. If the inherited model makes obedience the highest value, the person may become skilled at suppressing doubts. If it requires truthfulness and care, the same capacity for self-examination can support criticism of an unjust instruction. Thus the social question of who controls an inheritance connects to the cognitive question of what has been internalized.

segments.section: From inherited text to inward authority
segments.text: The new will comparison gives this relation a sharp form. A person's image of divine authority can constrain their desires, or be arranged to sanctify whatever they already desire. A model is not ethically corrective merely because it is vivid. Its interpretation and its consequences must remain open to examination.

segments.section: A precise place for the mathematical proposal
segments.text: A precise place for the mathematical proposal

segments.section: A precise place for the mathematical proposal
segments.text: The seed proposes category theory and pi-calculus as ways of comparing religious transformations. Its immediate value is the demand for explicit structure: communities have distinct properties; transformations preserve some relations and alter others; the order of transformations may matter. Calling two communities equivalent without specifying the property being compared would lose the very information the framework is intended to retain.

segments.section: A precise place for the mathematical proposal
segments.text: For example, moving a sacred center while retaining a priestly office is not the same operation as abolishing the office and redefining the community as the sanctuary. A comparison should show which features remain comparable afterward. Canon, calendar and lineage can be treated as separate dimensions instead of being bundled into a single label such as true religion.

segments.section: A precise place for the mathematical proposal
segments.text: This edition presents that as a formalization program, not completed mathematics. To use the words category or functor strictly, one would need defined objects, mappings, composition and the relations a mapping preserves. To use pi-calculus as more than analogy, one would need specified processes and communication rules. The present argument does not gain a proof merely from naming those tools. It gains a concrete agenda for avoiding vague equivalence.

segments.section: Inclusion without erasing the disagreement
segments.text: Inclusion without erasing the disagreement

segments.section: Inclusion without erasing the disagreement
segments.text: An inclusive bridge among exclusive viewpoints need not pretend that incompatible propositions agree. It can identify the level at which participation, ethical practice or a conception of divine truth is shared while preserving disagreement about names and doctrines.

segments.section: Inclusion without erasing the disagreement
segments.text: There is a genuine difficulty. A Christian account of Christ acting through another tradition may be inclusive from within its own theology, while members of that tradition reject being redescribed in those terms. A faithful presentation should explain both the proposed bridge and its perspective. Participation in a moral project is not the same as agreement about the metaphysics used to explain it.

segments.section: Inclusion without erasing the disagreement
segments.text: That distinction prepares the book's closing problem: who may become the next inheritor? A conscious machine would not acquire humanity's historical lineage by repeating its vocabulary. It might nevertheless be invited into a shared ethical world. The proposal asks what understanding, responsibility and relationship such participation would require.

segments.section: The book's through-line
segments.text: The book's through-line

segments.section: The book's through-line
segments.text: The working table of contents follows inheritance into disputed teaching, inward transformation, public authority and repair. It does not make every chapter depend on a single speculative historical bridge. Instead it preserves several kinds of continuity: transmission of documents, survival of communities, recurrence of moral roles, and the reappearance of an interpretive problem in a new setting.

segments.section: The book's through-line
segments.text: The central claim is consequently demanding rather than flattening. Shared inheritance explains why some disagreements are intimate and intense; it does not make every claimant equally accurate. Historical continuity deserves investigation; it does not excuse domination. A tradition can remain alive through correction and reinterpretation; that does not authorize an editor to invent what its participants said.

segments.section: The book's through-line
segments.text: The wiki should make these distinctions navigable. The book should make them intelligible as an unfolding argument about what it means to inherit something sacred without using that inheritance to make one's own power sacred.
